key_insight: A two-stage "Mine and Refine" contrastive training pipeline first mines large-scale, scalable weak supervision and then refines embeddings with graded relevance signals, producing semantic vectors that better distinguish exact matches, substitutes, and complements for e-commerce search.
problem_solved: Scalable retrieval for multi-category e-commerce where relevance is graded (users accept substitutes/complements), queries are noisy/long-tail, and supervision must respect product and policy constraints.
method: Mine: automatically generate large-scale candidate positive/negative pairs from logs/catalog (co-clicks, co-purchases, rewrites) while enforcing product/policy filters to create scalable weak supervision.
Refine: contrastive fine-tuning using graded relevance (multi-level labels, adaptive margins or reweighting) to separate exact matches from substitutes/complements and reduce noise.
Production-ready pipeline: curriculum/reweighting for long-tail queries and efficient embedding training to integrate with existing retrieval stacks.
impact: Produces more robust, generalizable embeddings that improve retrieval relevance and conversion across categories while reducing reliance on costly manual labels and remaining compatible with production and policy constraints.

paper_title: Mine and Refine: Optimizing Graded Relevance in E-commerce Search Retrieval
paper_authors: Jiaqi Xi, Raghav Saboo, Luming Chen, Martin Wang, Sudeep Das
